dataset: LLMRouterBench Performance Setting (20 small models, 15 datasets)

iteration2.description: Hyperparameter sweep — adaptive k, top_k x beta, improved confidence
key_findings: top_k=8, beta=8.0 is the best combination

iteration3.description: Final push — higher k, score-based routing, shrinkage
key_findings: Score-based routing is worse than rank-based (0.7153 vs 0.7326 at same k)
Empirical Bayes shrinkage doesn't help (best k0=1 → 0.7163)
Rank-based scoring naturally normalizes across heterogeneous clusters

key_insights: 1. MORE CLUSTERS WIN: k=183 (50 prompts/cluster) beats k=32 by 1.76%. The existing baseline was under-clustered.
2. WIDER NEIGHBORHOOD: top_k=8 (vs 5) blends more cluster opinions, reduces variance.
3. MODERATE TEMPERATURE: beta=8.0 (vs 10) gives softer weighting, prevents overconfidence.
4. RANK > SCORE: 1/rank scoring naturally normalizes across clusters with different score distributions. Mean scores are biased by cluster composition.
5. CONFIDENCE DOESN'T HELP: Falling back to best-single loses routing advantage. Even noisy cluster predictions beat best-single on OOD queries.
6. ENSEMBLE EMBEDDINGS DON'T HELP: all-mpnet, all-MiniLM, paraphrase-MiniLM are too correlated. Learned weights end up near-uniform (33/34/33%).
7. SHRINKAGE DOESN'T HELP: With k=183, most clusters have 40-60 samples — enough for reliable means. Shrinkage only helps for tiny clusters.
8. SCORE-BASED < RANK-BASED: Direct mean blending is sensitive to cluster heterogeneity. Rank-based is robust because it only cares about relative ordering.
what_didnt_work: Confidence-aware fallback (V1, V2, V3) — all variants underperform baseline
Multi-embedder ensemble — embedders too correlated, no diversity gain
Empirical Bayes shrinkage — clusters large enough that shrinkage adds bias
Score-based routing — mean scores biased by cluster composition
Hybrid approaches — combining orthogonal ideas diluted each signal
recommendations: Production: Use k=183, top_k=8, beta=8.0 with rank-based scoring. Simple, fast (0.8s for 2297 queries), and beats all baselines.
The existing production router's k=16 is too conservative for this data size. Scale k with corpus.
Focus on data quality and coverage rather than algorithm complexity — the biggest wins came from better hyperparameters, not new algorithms.
Confidence scoring would be more useful in a cost-aware setting (route cheap models when confident, expensive when uncertain) — not explored here.
